item.title: Scottish athlete won her country a medal at the Commonwealth Games, but had to return to her McDonald's job days later
item.description: Scottish judoka Summer Shaw made headlines by winning a bronze medal at the Commonwealth Games, only to head back to her part-time McDonald's job to make ends meet for her sporting endeavors. Her engaging TikTok video on the matter caught widespread interest, highlighting her need for further financial support. Eager for sponsorship, she dreams of fully committing to her judo career.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: GTA 6 Release: Kai Cenat dodges every alleged leak; vows to 100% game first
item.description: Kai Cenat says he has not watched any GTA 6 leaks because he is “committed to the actual game.” During his August 22 livestream, he also promised to become the first person ever to 100% GTA 6. The streamer previously said he could spend unlimited time playing after launch. With GTA 6 arriving in November 2026, Cenat already has his challenge planned.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: In 1900, JP Morgan bought 117 acres for daughter's wedding; land later went to Acadia National Park
item.description: A stretch of Maine coastline that was once part of a wealthy family’s private summer estate is now open to visitors as part of Acadia National Park. The land was donated in 1949 by Eleanor Morgan Satterlee in memory of her mother, Louisa, after the family property was badly damaged in the 1947 fire.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: HasanAbi vs xQc and Asmongold: Hasanabi calls streamers "worm-like" over Charlie Kirk song
item.description: HasanAbi has fired back at xQc, Asmongold, Destiny and others after they criticized his appearance singing the “We Are Charlie Kirk” song. During an August 23 livestream, Hasan called his critics “worm-like individuals” and “opportunists,” while accusing them of farming outrage and relying on algorithm-driven drama. He also argued that the backlash showed a clear double standard around political jokes and criticism.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: ISS cricket experiment found microgravity-exposed larvae hatched earlier than ground controls
item.description: In 2005, scientists examined cricket reproduction on the International Space Station, where embryos grew under microgravity conditions. Interestingly, larvae emerged sooner than those on Earth, suggesting that microgravity affects developmental speed while preserving key neural structures. This research is vital for comprehending how life forms adjust to lesser gravitational forces, expanding our knowledge of development beyond Earth.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Meet Iris Shen, the 17-year-old Texas student who tested potential blood-cancer drugs in clams and her research won $150,000
item.description: A talented teen from Texas, Iris Shen, has triumphed in a renowned science contest with her groundbreaking research. By investigating a potential cancer treatment using clams, she discovered that these creatures exhibit effects akin to human cells. Her innovative work highlights marine bivalves as a viable and ethical alternative for animal testing, directly tackling the pressing ethical and financial challenges associated with conventional methods.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Freezing liquid inside optical fibre makes light and sound interact 1,000 times more strongly
item.description: Scientists have frozen the liquid inside a special optical fibre to -196°C, creating conditions where light and sound interact more than 1,000 times more strongly than in ordinary fibres. The team found that the frozen fibre could still guide light and hypersonic sound waves. The breakthrough also helped researchers demonstrate optoacoustic memory, which could have potential applications in lower-energy photonic computing, quantum information processing and high-precision sensing.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Doja Cat steps in to support Nitro Camden after his shocking viral moment with his mom
item.description: Doja Cat has stepped up to uplift Twitch streamer Nitro Camden following a tough situation that caught public attention. She encouraged him to chase his aspirations and urged fans to show their support by subscribing. Camden's streaming journey took a leap after a huge raid by a renowned creator, leading to his partnership with various platforms and a surge in followers.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Asmongold Considers Twitch Exit: Destiny warns it’s Hasan’s dream; Rumble, Kick and YouTube loom
item.description: Asmongold is considering leaving Twitch if he receives another suspension after his recent 14-day ban. Destiny reacted to the possibility by saying it would be “Hasan’s dream,” arguing that Hasan could gain “sole reign” over the platform. Asmongold has mentioned Kick, Rumble and YouTube as possible alternatives, but he has not confirmed that he is leaving Twitch.

item.title: After Australia, New Zealand proposes social media ban for under 16
item.description: New Zealand's Prime Minister Christopher Luxon proposed banning children under sixteen from social media. This legislation aims to protect young people from harmful online content and addictive technologies. However, two coalition parties oppose the bill, which may require opposition support to pass. Australia enacted a similar ban in December 2025, with other nations considering such measures. New Zealand also banned mobile phones in schools for all students during the day.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Invasive Argentine ants are defending other pests in California, troubling farmers and leaving natives hungry
item.description: Invasive Argentine ants have formed a unique symbiotic relationship with sap-feeding insects, creating challenges for citrus groves and vineyards. First spotted in the U.S. in 1891, their expansion is aided by California's favorable climate and human activity. To effectively manage the situation, it's crucial to tackle both the ant populations and their pest partners as interconnected issues.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Henderson Island rats survived a 75-tonne poison campaign and rebounded within two years
item.description: Conservationists attempted a large-scale rat eradication on Henderson Island in 2011. About seventy-five tonnes of poisoned bait were spread across the remote South Pacific island. However, a small number of rats survived the intensive campaign. Within two years, the rat population had recovered significantly to former levels. This event underscores the difficulty of achieving complete eradication and the resilience of invasive species.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Massachusetts crew lands 1,260-pound blue marlin, misses world record
item.description: In a thrilling encounter off Cape Cod, a charter captain teamed up with an angler to reel in an astonishing blue marlin that tipped the scales at 1,260 pounds and stretched over eleven feet. This remarkable catch approached the Atlantic blue marlin world record from 1992, prompting researchers to investigate its head to gauge its age. After the impressive capture, the fish was generously shared among several admirers.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Four medaka fish flew into space in 1994; 43 eggs were laid and eight baby fish hatched
item.description: Astronaut Chiaki Mukai took four medaka fish into space in July 1994 as part of an experiment to study reproduction in microgravity. The fish laid eggs during the mission, with eight of 43 identified eggs hatching in space. After returning to Earth, the adult fish gradually recovered, while the young “space medaka” continued to grow normally.

item.title: US sailor’s father detained by ICE while son serves aboard USS Abraham Lincoln
item.description: A US sailor's father, originally from Nicaragua, faced immigration officials' detention during a routine vehicle stop in Key West, Florida. While his son serves overseas, he feels deep concern for his father's situation, who is currently waiting for green card approval and possesses identification. This incident has raised eyebrows amid heightened scrutiny surrounding the USS Abraham Lincoln's prolonged deployment.
